mappings.note: Knowing which crop is transplanted matches a crop to a sowing practice that raises yield. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the crop is not being placed in a seasonal class.
Hepatitis B traced to its causative organism is a disease-to-cause link. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, since no useful/harmful sorting is asked for.
Recognising viruses as the group on the living/non-living borderline is a classification by characteristics. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, because a group is placed rather than a process explained.
A legume needing no nitrogenous fertiliser is the controlled-use-of-fertilisers judgement. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, which fits the mechanism items; here the pupil acts on it by withholding an input.
Naming the bacterium that turns alcohol into acetic acid identifies a useful microorganism. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-2, used for the fermentation item where the chemical change is the question.
Picking the bacterial disease links an illness to the kind of agent behind it. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, because the options are diseases, not organisms.
Reading leaf-spot symptoms back to a disease and its agent is cause-finding from evidence. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, since the observations are given and no investigation is conducted.
Explaining why beans thrive in nitrogen-poor soil via Rhizobium nodules is causal reasoning. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1: a reason is asked for, not a fertiliser decision.
Yeast used in bread or alcohol production is the useful side of the microorganism classification. Not C-SCI3.2-LO-1, because the product is named rather than a home application asked for.
Who discovered Bacillus anthracis is a story of scientific discovery, the only outcome in the frame covering the history of science. Not C-SCI1.2-LO-1, since no organism is classified.
Excluding the non-protozoan from a list sorts microorganisms into their groups. Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, because no disease is being traced.
